chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithamī from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb from Ismā'īl ibn Najīḥ al-Rammāḥ who said:
We were with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) in Mina on one of the nights, so he said: 'What are these people saying regarding [the verse]
So whoever hastens [his departure] in two days, there is no sin upon him, and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him

So whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him, indeed there is no sin upon him, and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him, indeed there is no sin upon him for the one who fears [God]. It is for you all, and the people are the multitude, and you are the pilgrims.

key_terms.لِمَنِ اتَّقَى: For the one who fears God (taqwa)
key_terms.يَوْمَيْنِ: Two days (referring to the 11th and 12th of Dhul-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: Who is permitted to leave Mina early or stay late during Hajj according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) refutes the prevailing view that the Quranic permission for hastening or delaying departure from Mina was restricted by social status—specifically, that it applied only to Bedouins or city dwellers respectively. He clarifies that the phrase 'for those who fear' (liman ittaqa) refers to all pilgrims, establishing that the flexibility in timing is a universal concession for the entire community of Hajj, regardless of their background.
